introduction.zh: 十二月的一个寒夜，大家围着厨房的炉火，听医生念他自己写的动物语故事。猫头鹰图图忽然竖起耳朵：外面有动静。这样冷的夜里，谁会在外面奔跑？
introduction.en: A cold December night. Everyone sits round the kitchen fire while the Doctor reads aloud from books he wrote himself in animal-language. Suddenly the owl lifts its head: there is a noise outside. Who would be running about on such a night?

sentences: 那个冬天非常冷。
十二月的一个晚上，大家都围坐在厨房暖烘烘的炉火旁，医生正大声念他自己用动物语写的书给他们听，这时猫头鹰图图忽然说：

hints.zh: 图图，医生的猫头鹰。
hints.en: Too-Too, the Doctor's owl.

sentences: 外面那是什么声音？」
大家都侧耳去听；不一会儿，他们听见有人奔跑的声音。
接着门猛地被推开，猴子奇奇跑了进来，喘得上气不接下气。

hints.zh: 奇奇，那只猴子。
hints.en: Chee-Chee, the monkey.

sentences: 「医生！」他喊道，「我刚收到非洲一位表亲捎来的消息。
那边的猴子中间正闹一种可怕的病。
它们一个接一个染上——成百成百地死去。
它们听说过你，求你到非洲去，把这场病止住。」
「消息是谁带来的？」医生问，一边摘下眼镜，放下了书。
「一只燕子。」奇奇说。
「她就在外面，站在接雨水的桶上。」

hints.zh: 接雨水的大桶，放在屋外接屋檐流下来的雨水。
hints.en: A big barrel outside that catches rain-water from the roof.

sentences: 「把她带到火边来。」医生说。
「她一定冻坏了。
燕子六个星期前就飞到南方去了！」

hints.zh: 这里不是「死了」，是「冻得受不了」，口语里夸张的说法。
hints.en: Here it means "half frozen", not "dead": a strong everyday exaggeration.

sentences: 于是燕子被带了进来，缩成一团，瑟瑟发抖；她起初还有点害怕，但很快就暖和过来，落在壁炉架的边上，开始说话了。

quiz.question: What news does Chee-Chee bring from Africa?
options: The monkeys there have found a new king.
The monkeys there are dying of a terrible sickness.
The Doctor's cousin is coming to England.

feedback.zh: 奇奇说非洲的猴子中间正闹一种可怕的病，它们成百成百地死去，所以才来求医生去止住它。
feedback.en: Chee-Chee reports a terrible sickness among the monkeys out there: they are catching it and dying in hundreds.

quiz.question: What is the Doctor doing as he asks who brought the message?
options: Packing a bag for the journey.
Lighting the kitchen fire.
Taking off his spectacles and laying down his book.

feedback.zh: 原文写他一边摘下眼镜、放下书，一边问「消息是谁带来的」。
feedback.en: He takes off his spectacles and lays down his book as he asks the question.

grammar.excerpt: when they were all sitting round the warm fire in the kitchen, and the Doctor was reading aloud to them

focus.zh: when 从句用过去进行时 were sitting、was reading 铺开背景：大家正坐着听书，事情就在这时发生。
focus.en: The when-clause uses the past continuous (were sitting, was reading) to set the scene before something else happens.

introduction.zh: 非洲在等着，可医生的话很明白：他连船票都买不起。奇奇被派去取存钱盒，那里头究竟还剩多少？一个连两便士都留不住的人，要怎么渡海？
introduction.en: Africa is waiting, but the Doctor has a plain problem: he cannot even pay for the tickets. Chee-Chee is sent to fetch the money-box. How much is still inside it, and how does a man with no money reach the sea?

sentences: 她说完，医生说：
「我很愿意去非洲——尤其是这样的冷天。
可我怕我们钱不够买船票。
把存钱盒给我拿来，奇奇。」
于是猴子爬上去，把它从餐具柜最上层取了下来。

hints.zh: 厨房里的餐具柜、碗柜；不是卧室里的梳妆台。
hints.en: A kitchen cupboard for dishes, not a bedroom dressing-table.

sentences: 里面什么也没有——连一个便士都没有！
「我原以为里头还剩两便士呢。」医生说。

hints.zh: 两便士，英国旧币制里的铜币，是很少的一点钱。
hints.en: Twopence: two old British pennies, a very small sum.

sentences: 「本来是有的。」猫头鹰说。
「可你拿它给那只獾的娃娃买了个摇铃，那会儿他正长牙。」

hints.zh: 婴儿玩的摇铃、拨浪鼓，一摇就响，长牙的孩子常拿着啃。
hints.en: A baby's rattle: a toy that makes a noise when it is shaken.

sentences: 「是吗？」医生说，「天哪，天哪！
钱这东西，真是麻烦！
好吧，算了。
也许我下到海边去，能借到一条送我们去非洲的船。
我认识一个水手，他有一次抱了娃娃来找我看麻疹。
也许他肯把船借给我们——那娃娃后来好了。」
于是第二天一大早，医生就下到海边去了。
他回来的时候告诉动物们事情办成了——那个水手愿意把船借给他们。
于是鳄鱼、猴子和鹦鹉都高兴起来，唱起了歌，因为它们要回非洲去了，那是它们真正的家。
医生却说：

quiz.question: Why is there no money in the money-box?
options: The Doctor spent it on a rattle for the badger's baby.
Chee-Chee took it with him to Africa.
It was lost in the snow outside.

feedback.zh: 猫头鹰说，那点钱被医生拿去给獾的娃娃买摇铃了，因为那孩子正在长牙。
feedback.en: The owl explains that the money went on a rattle for the badger's baby, who was teething.

quiz.question: How does the Doctor hope to get a boat?
options: He will buy one with his savings.
The Cat's-meat-Man will give him one.
A sailor whose baby he once cured may lend him one.

feedback.zh: 医生提起一个抱着娃娃来看麻疹的水手，希望那人肯借船——那孩子后来好了。
feedback.en: He remembers a seaman whose baby he cured of measles, and hopes the man will lend him his boat.

grammar.excerpt: if I go down to the seaside I shall be able to borrow a boat

focus.zh: if 从句讲的是将来的事，动词却用一般现在时 go；主句才用 shall be able to。从句里不加 will。
focus.en: The if-clause talks about the future but keeps the present tense go; the main clause carries shall be able to.

title.en: What to Take on a Ship

introduction.zh: 能上船的只有几位，其余动物要在冬天回田野里去。鹦鹉波利尼西亚远航过多次，开始一样样清点船上必备的东西：硬饼干、罐头牛肉、锚，还有一只铃铛。船上的铃铛到底是做什么用的？
introduction.en: Only a few animals can go; the rest go back to the fields for the winter. The parrot Polynesia has made long voyages, so she lists what the ship must carry: hard biscuit, tins of beef, an anchor — and a bell. What could a ship want with a bell?

sentences: 「我只能带你们三个——再加上狗吉普、鸭子达布达布、小猪咕咕和猫头鹰图图。
其余的动物，像睡鼠、水田鼠和蝙蝠，只好回到它们出生的田野里去住，等我们回家。
不过它们大多数整个冬天都在睡觉，不会在意这件事——再说，去非洲对它们也不好。」

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor's dog.

hints.zh: 达布达布，医生的鸭子。
hints.en: Dab-Dab, the Doctor's duck.

hints.zh: 咕咕，医生的小猪。
hints.en: Gub-Gub, the Doctor's pig.

sentences: 于是，那只出过许多次远洋的鹦鹉，开始告诉医生这趟上船他得带上哪些东西。
「你得带足硬面包，」她说，「他们管它叫『硬饼干』。
还得有罐头牛肉——外加一只锚。」

hints.zh: 船员吃的硬面饼，烤得很干、放得久不坏，也叫 hard tack（硬饼干）。
hints.en: Pilot-bread, or hard tack: a hard dry biscuit that keeps for months at sea.

sentences: 「我想船自己会带锚吧。」医生说。
「那就看清楚了。」波利尼西亚说。
「因为这很要紧。
没有锚，船就停不下来。
你还需要一只铃铛。」

hints.zh: 波利尼西亚，医生的鹦鹉；她出过远门，懂航海。
hints.en: Polynesia, the Doctor's parrot, who has been on long voyages before.

sentences: 「那要它做什么？」医生问。
「用来报时间呀。」鹦鹉说。
「你每隔半小时去敲一敲，就知道现在是什么时辰。
再多带些绳子——出海的时候，绳子总派得上用场。」

hints.zh: 派得上用场、迟早用得上；不是「拿在手里」。
hints.en: Comes in handy: turns out to be useful when you need it.

sentences: 接着他们开始发愁：买这些东西的钱，该到哪里去弄。

quiz.question: Why will most of the animals go back to the fields?
options: There is not enough room for them on the ship.
They are afraid of going on the water.
Most of them sleep through the winter, and Africa would not suit them.

feedback.zh: 医生说它们大多整个冬天都在睡觉，不会在意；再说，去非洲对它们也不好。
feedback.en: The Doctor says most of them sleep through the winter so they will not mind, and Africa would not be good for them.

quiz.question: Why does Polynesia say they need a bell?
options: To tell the time by, ringing it every half-hour.
To call the animals to their meals.
To warn other ships in the dark.

feedback.zh: 她说每隔半小时去敲一次铃，就知道现在是什么时辰了。
feedback.en: She says you ring it every half-hour, and then you know what time it is.

grammar.excerpt: it wouldn’t be good for them to go to Africa

focus.zh: for them 是不定式 to go 的逻辑主语：对他们来说，去非洲不好；for 后面用宾格 them。
focus.en: For them is the logical subject of to go: going to Africa would not be good for them.

title.en: The Key for the Old Horse

introduction.zh: 又是因为钱。医生气得直嚷嚷，非得派人去跟杂货店老板谈。房子要关起来，行李要搬下海边，家里还有一位老住户走不了——钥匙该交给谁？
introduction.en: Money again. The Doctor shouts in anger, and someone must go and talk to the grocer. The house is to be shut up, the luggage carried down to the sea, and one old resident cannot go with them. Who should have the key?

sentences: 「唉，真烦人！
又是钱。」医生叫起来。
「天哪！
到了非洲我就高兴了，在那儿我们根本不用花钱！
我去问问杂货店老板，能不能等我回来再付钱——不，我让水手去问他。」
于是水手去见杂货店老板。
不久，他就带着他们要的各样东西回来了。
接着动物们收拾行李；他们关掉水阀，免得管子冻裂，又装上护窗板，然后把房子锁好，把钥匙交给住在马厩里的那匹老马。
等他们看清阁楼里的干草足够老马吃上一冬，就把全部行李搬到海边，上了船。

hints.zh: 护窗板，钉在窗外的木挡板，主人出远门时装上，防风防贼。
hints.en: Wooden boards fixed over the windows when a house is left empty.

hints.zh: 阁楼、草料棚，马厩上面堆放干草的地方。
hints.en: The loft: the space above the stable where hay is stored.

sentences: 卖猫食的人也来送行；他给医生带来一个很大的板油布丁作礼物，因为他说，他听人讲外国买不到板油布丁。

hints.zh: 卖猫食的人，走街串巷卖马肉、猫食的小贩。
hints.en: The cat's-meat man: a street seller who sold meat for cats and dogs.

hints.zh: 板油布丁，用牛油和面做的英国传统点心，冬天常吃。
hints.en: Suet pudding: a heavy traditional British pudding made with beef fat.

sentences: 他们一上船，小猪咕咕就问床在哪儿，因为当时是下午四点，他想睡午觉了。
于是波利尼西亚带他下到船肚子里，指给他看那些床——它们一张摞一张，像靠墙的书架。

quiz.question: What do they do with the key of the house?
options: They leave it with the Cat's-meat-Man.
They give it to the old horse in the stable.
They hang it inside the front door.

feedback.zh: 他们把房子锁好，钥匙交给住在马厩里的那匹老马，还请它看家。
feedback.en: They lock the house and give the key to the old horse who lives in the stable.

quiz.question: Why does the Cat's-meat-Man bring a suet-pudding?
options: He has been told you cannot get them in foreign parts.
The Doctor asked him to buy one for the voyage.
It is a present for Gub-Gub, who likes puddings.

feedback.zh: 他说他听人讲，到了外国就买不到板油布丁了，所以带一个来送给医生。
feedback.en: He says he has been told that suet-puddings cannot be got in foreign parts.

grammar.excerpt: As soon as they were on the ship

focus.zh: as soon as 引导时间从句，意思是「一……就……」；主句 asked 用一般过去时，两件事紧接着发生。
focus.en: As soon as introduces the time clause: the moment they were on the ship, Gub-Gub asked.

introduction.zh: 行李都搬上了船，咕咕被领到船肚子里看他的床。他站在那儿，怎么也不肯相信这东西是给人睡的。船就要开了，可这一船人和动物里，谁认得去非洲的路？
introduction.en: The luggage is on board, and Gub-Gub is taken down inside the ship to see his bed. He stands and stares: he will not believe that anyone could sleep in it. The ship is about to sail — but who on board knows the road to Africa?

sentences: 「哎呀，这哪是床！」咕咕叫起来。
「这是个架子！」
「船上的床都是这样的。」鹦鹉说。
「这不是架子。
爬上去睡就是了。
这个呀，就叫『铺位』。」

hints.zh: 铺位，船上或宿舍里固定在墙上的窄床，常常上下叠放。
hints.en: A bunk: a narrow fixed bed on a ship, often one of two stacked together.

sentences: 「我看我还是先不睡了。」咕咕说。
「我太兴奋了。
我想再上去，看他们开船。」

hints.zh: 看他们开船；start 在这里是「出发」，不是「开始做某事」。
hints.en: See them start: watch the ship set off; start here means "set out".

sentences: 「也难怪，这是你头一回出海。」波利尼西亚说。
「过些日子，你就习惯这种日子了。」
她一边沿着船梯往上走，一边自己哼着这首歌：

hints.zh: 慢慢习惯这种生活；get used to 是「变得习惯」，跟表示「过去常常」的 used to 不是一回事。
hints.en: Get used to the life means become accustomed to it — not the same as "used to do", which talks about past habits.

sentences: 我见过黑海，也见过红海；我绕过怀特岛；我发现了黄河，还有橙河——都是在夜里。
如今格陵兰又退到身后，我航行在蓝色的大洋上。
简，这些颜色我都看厌了，所以我要回到你身边。

hints.zh: 怀特岛，英格兰南岸外的小岛，船出海时常从它旁边经过。
hints.en: The Isle of Wight: a small island off the south coast of England.

hints.zh: 简，歌里水手思念的姑娘，是泛指的，不是这本书里的人物。
hints.en: Jane is the sailor's sweetheart in the song — not a character in this book.

sentences: 他们正要启程，医生却说，他得回去问问水手去非洲怎么走。
可燕子说，那个国家她去过很多次，愿意指给他们看怎么走。
于是医生让奇奇把锚拉上来，航行就这样开始了。

quiz.question: What does Gub-Gub think of the bed on the ship?
options: He thinks it is too small for him.
He thinks it is a table for the animals.
He thinks it is a shelf.

feedback.zh: 咕咕一看就叫起来：这哪是床，这是个架子；鹦鹉只好告诉他，船上管这个叫「铺位」。
feedback.en: Gub-Gub cries that it is not a bed at all but a shelf; the parrot has to explain that it is called a bunk.

quiz.question: Who says she can show them the way to Africa?
options: The sailor.
The swallow.
Polynesia.

feedback.zh: 医生本来还想回去问水手，燕子说那个国家她去过很多次，愿意带路。
feedback.en: The Doctor was going back to ask the sailor, but the swallow says she has been there many times and will show them the way.

grammar.excerpt: They were just going to start on their journey

focus.zh: were going to start 是过去的打算：他们正要出发；just 强调「就差一点」，when 从句随即打断。
focus.en: Were going to start is a plan in the past: they were just about to leave when something interrupted them.
